tasks.description:
**Which of two looks held the stripes?** Each trial shows the observer two looks in turn, each [[param:interval_duration]] long and [[param:isi]] apart, marked by four corner marks around a square field of [[param:field_dva]] on a uniform grey. In one look, chosen at random, the field holds a stationary vertical sine-wave grating at the same mean luminance as the grey; in the other it holds nothing. The observer presses F for the first look or J for the second; the fixation point then turns green or red for [[param:feedback_duration]].

**What changes.** The spatial frequency (cycles per degree, one cell each, interleaved) and, trial by trial, the grating's contrast (Lmax - Lmin) / (Lmax + Lmin), which QUEST+ chooses on a log scale to home in on each cell's threshold.

**What is measured.** Proportion correct as a function of contrast in each cell; the threshold is the contrast for 81% correct in a fitted Weibull function, and the contrast sensitivity is 1 / threshold. Plotted against spatial frequency, sensitivities form the contrast-sensitivity function. The record keeps the contrast asked for and the contrast of the image actually drawn.

**What it can and cannot show.** A drop in sensitivity at low and high frequencies, with a peak between, for this observer on this display. Its absolute values depend on the display's luminance, gamma and bit depth, the field size and the observer's optics; it is not a clinical test. The paper measured thresholds by adjustment ([[task:csf-adjustment]]); forced choice is a deliberate change.
notes: Paper (p. 553): mean 500 cd/m2, contrast switched on and off at 0.5 c/s, 10 x 10 or 2 x 2 cm apertures at 57 or 285 cm (10 or 2 deg), monocular, cycloplegic, 2.5-mm artificial pupil, threshold by adjustment, 5 or 10 settings.
Changed here: two-interval forced choice with QUEST+, binocular natural viewing, a display's luminance instead of 500 cd/m2.
ASSUMED: frequencies, vertical stripes, random phase, 1000-ms looks, 500-ms gap, corner marks, fixation point, feedback, QUEST+ grids, 60 trials per cell.
Contrast below one display code step (about 0.8% on 8 bits) exists only through dithering; set display_bits and measure gamma before real data.

tasks.description:
**The high-frequency set.** The same two-look trial as the main set: corner marks show two looks of [[param:interval_duration]], [[param:isi]] apart; a stationary vertical sine grating is in one, chosen at random; F for the first, J for the second. The field is the paper's small aperture, [[param:field_dva]] on a side, and the frequencies run from 2 to 22.6 c/deg, the part of Fig. 2 the paper measured from 285 cm.

**Why it needs its own rig.** A pixel display can only draw a grating with enough pixels per cycle; this task refuses any frequency with fewer than [[param:min_px_per_cycle]]. At 22.6 c/deg that means about 90 px/deg: the example booth panel viewed from 150 cm (configs/rig-booth-far.yaml), not from 57 cm (36 px/deg), where the session stops before the first trial and names the frequencies it cannot show. Even when allowed, a display's own blur lowers the contrast it delivers near its limit, which this folder does not measure.

**What is measured.** As in the main set: a threshold (81% correct in a fitted Weibull) and its reciprocal, the sensitivity, per frequency. The paper found that a 2 deg field lowers sensitivity below about 3 c/deg compared with a 10 deg field (p. 554), so the two sets are not interchangeable at their overlapping frequencies.
notes: Paper (pp. 553-554, Fig. 2): the 2 x 2 deg field was a 2 x 2 cm aperture at 57 cm or 10 x 10 cm at 285 cm; the high frequencies came from 285 cm because the tube lost contrast above 10 c/cm.
Here: 2 deg field at 2, 4, 8, 16 and 22.6 c/deg (ASSUMED levels); refused unless every frequency gets 4 px per cycle on the rig (about 90 px/deg at 22.6 c/deg).
Drawing: the 2 deg field to scale with one example frequency, 4 c/deg, at an illustrative contrast of 0.6; the timing is the same as the main set's.

tasks.description:
**The paper's Fourier test.** The same two-look trial as the main set in the [[param:field_dva]] field, but each frequency is measured with two waveforms, interleaved: a sine-wave grating and a square-wave grating of the same period. A trial shows ONE of them, in one of the two looks; the drawing shows the square wave, which steps between two levels at the same mean.

**Why the ratio is 4/pi.** A square wave of contrast m is a sum of sine waves at f, 3f, 5f, ...; its fundamental has amplitude 4m/pi. If only the fundamental decides whether the grating is seen, square-wave sensitivity is 4/pi = 1.273 times sine-wave sensitivity; the paper found that above about 0.8 c/deg and a larger ratio below it (pp. 555-556). Each trial records the square wave's contrast and its drawn fundamental.

**Sampling.** A square wave needs its harmonics drawn too, so its frequencies are refused below [[param:square_min_px_per_cycle]] px per cycle (third harmonic at 4 or more); on the example booth that caps the set at 3 c/deg. Above that, the display's pixels rather than the eye would remove the harmonics and the ratio would say nothing about vision.
notes: Paper (pp. 555-556, Figs. 3-4): square/sine sensitivity ratio 4/pi = 1.273 above about 0.8 c/deg (1.280 +/- 0.025 for F.W.C. over 1-35 c/deg), larger below; thresholds for the two waveforms measured alternately.
Here: sine and square interleaved at 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 c/deg (ASSUMED levels); square waves refused below 12 px per cycle; the analysis reports the ratio per frequency beside 4/pi.
Drawing: the square wave at 1 c/deg, contrast 0.6 (illustrative); sine trials look like the main set's drawing. One waveform per trial, never both.

tasks.description:
**The paper's method.** The grating switches on and off once every [[param:flicker_period]] (the paper's 0.5 c/s) inside a square field of [[param:field_dva]], with no change in mean luminance. The observer turns its contrast down or up (arrow keys or scroll wheel, a factor of 10^[[param:knob_step_log10]] per step) until the stripes are barely detectable, then presses SPACE. Each spatial frequency gets [[param:paradigm.n_per_condition]] settings, in random order, each starting from a random contrast.

**What is measured.** The settings; a frequency's threshold is their geometric mean and the sensitivity its reciprocal. Settings depend on the observer's criterion for "barely detectable", which forced choice ([[task:csf-2ifc]]) avoids.
notes: Paper (p. 553): on-off at 0.5 c/s, settings until barely detectable, 5 or 10 per threshold, standard error under 10%.
ASSUMED: equal on and off halves, the knob step, start contrasts, no fixation mark, 5 settings per frequency.
